title: Gradient descent, one step at a time
summary: How a model finds the bottom of its loss by taking small steps downhill.

scenes.heading: Gradient descent
scenes.subheading: How a model learns by walking downhill
scenes.narration: Every model you train has to answer one question. How do I change my numbers so I make fewer mistakes? Gradient descent is the answer almost every model uses.

scenes.heading: Loss
scenes.subheading: One number for how wrong the model is

items.text: Average error over the training data
items.detail: Lower is better. Zero means every prediction is right.

scenes.narration: First we need a way to measure mistakes. The loss is the average error over all the training data. When the loss goes down, the model is getting better.

scenes.heading: The idea
scenes.subheading: Think of the loss as a hill

items.text: Each setting of the weights is a spot on the hill

items.detail: It is the direction the loss grows fastest.

scenes.narration: Picture every possible setting of the weights as a spot on a hill, and the height is the loss. The gradient tells you which way is uphill. So to lower the loss, you take a step the other way.

scenes.heading: One step

items.detail: w = w - learning rate x gradient

items.text: Repeat until the loss stops falling

scenes.narration: Here is a single step. Compute the loss, then compute its gradient. Move every weight a little bit against the gradient. Then do it again, until the loss stops going down.

scenes.heading: The learning rate

items.detail: Safe, but it takes forever to reach the bottom.
It overshoots and bounces, or flies off the hill.

scenes.narration: The learning rate sets the size of each step. Make it too small, and training crawls. Make it too big, and you jump right over the bottom and bounce around, or even diverge.

scenes.heading: In code

items.text: The gradient of the mean squared error

scenes.code:
for epoch in range(1000):
    pred = X @ w
    grad = 2 * X.T @ (pred - y) / len(y)
    w = w - lr * grad
scenes.narration: Here is the whole thing in four lines. We predict, then compute the gradient of the mean squared error. Then we nudge the weights against it, a thousand times.

scenes.heading: What to remember

items.text: Loss measures how wrong you are
Step downhill, by the learning rate

scenes.narration: So, three things to remember. The loss measures how wrong you are. The gradient points uphill, and each step moves you downhill by an amount the learning rate decides.
